olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: 20 tennis players scheduled exactly 14 two-person games, each player in at least one game. Prove there is a set of 6 games involving 12 distinct players.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1989

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $P(z)=z^n+c_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+c_n$ with real $c_k$, and $|P(i)|<1$. Prove there exist real $a,b$ with $P(a+bi)=0$ and $(a^2+b^2+1)^2<4b^2+1$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1989

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$ with $AB<AC<BC$; $I$ = incenter, $O$ = circumcenter. Prove line $IO$ intersects segments $AB$ and $BC$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1989

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $u,v$ be real with $(u+u^2+\cdots+u^8)+10u^9=(v+v^2+\cdots+v^{10})+10v^{11}=8$. Determine which of $u,v$ is larger.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1989
